comparison.text: If every day were like today, you would live at 9.5x the WHO annual safe level.
comparison.source_name: WHO, 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines (PM2.5 annual average 5 ug/m3)
comparison.caveat: Compares one day against an annual guideline, so it describes a hypothetical year of days like today, not your actual annual exposure.

comparison.text: Official Indian AQI: 28 out of 500, category 'Good'. That is the government's own scale.
comparison.source_name: CPCB, National Air Quality Index (PM2.5 breakpoints)
comparison.caveat: Computed from PM2.5 alone. The full CPCB AQI takes the worst sub-index across pollutants, so the official city AQI can be higher on days another pollutant dominates.

comparison.text: Plot twist: 68 percent of outdoor air pollution deaths are heart disease and stroke. It was never just about your lungs.
comparison.source_name: WHO fact sheet, Ambient (outdoor) air quality and health
comparison.caveat: WHO's breakdown of premature deaths linked to outdoor air pollution: 68 percent ischaemic heart disease and stroke, 14 percent COPD, 14 percent acute lower respiratory infection, 4 percent lung cancer.

comparison.text: The most polluted city on Earth in the 2025 IQAir report is Loni, in Delhi NCR: 112.5 ug/m3 average, 22x the WHO limit. All 25 worst cities were in India, Pakistan and China.
comparison.source_name: IQAir, 2025 World Air Quality Report press release
comparison.caveat: IQAir rankings blend government and low-cost sensor data and only cover cities that measure at all. Plenty of unmonitored places never make the list.
